entries.reason: The noun every body name ends with: a society names a made being by what its body is, and every drafted body is some creature, whatever its maker calls it.

entries.words: what every body name is held to
entries.reason: A body name states at most two features and the noun: enough to tell most bodies in a town apart in a sentence a decider reads, short enough to read over a figure. Two bodies that share a name are told apart by number, as two beings of one kind are. A tail names nothing: most bodies have one.

entries.reason: More than one head is what anybody notices first, so it is named first, with how many.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica body names; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Wings are named next: every winged body has one or two pairs, and a pair or two reads the same from the ground, so they are not counted.

entries.reason: How many legs a body walks on tells a biped from a beast from a many-legged thing.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica body names; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Tentacles are named where legs do not already name the body, with how many.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica body names; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Arms tell a body that can carry in its hands from one that cannot.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica body names; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Fins are named after everything a body stands or carries with, uncounted, as wings are.

entries.reason: A body of six or more spine segments and no legs is mostly spine, as a serpentine body is by the body grammar's own bound, so its length is what names it.

entries.reason: A count as a word, so a body name is words and spaces alone, as every kind's label is. Twelve is the most of any one part a body recipe states (six pairs of legs, twelve tentacles).

entries.words: what a decider reads of the body

spec.lead: A creature about {length} long and {height} high

moves.still: It cannot move from where it is.

holds.jaws: It carries a thing in its jaws.
holds.hands: It carries things in its hands.
holds.front_claws: It carries things in its front claws.

entries.reason: A made being's summary, where a shipped kind's is written by hand: its size in metres, its parts by count in rank order, whether it walks and what it carries with, all from its body's own figures, so a decider knows what body it decides for and nothing a person wrote reaches a society.
